title: Project scope — spoken follow-up
situation: In a technical discussion, a stakeholder asks for five more features before the first milestone. You must answer aloud accurately without overstating the evidence.
instructions: Say aloud how you respond to five extra features before the first milestone, without refusing outright.

vocabulary.meaning: keeping the committed content of a milestone fixed by naming what leaves whenever something enters
an exchange stated out loud, which turns an unbounded request into a decision someone can take

expectedElements: The request is acknowledged rather than dismissed
The trade-off is stated in concrete terms
A decision is handed back to the requester
modelAnswer: I hear the request, and none of the five is unreasonable on its own. What I cannot do is add them and keep the milestone date, because the milestone is already sized to the time available. So the question I would hand back is which of the five matters most, and what comes out to make room for it. If the answer is that nothing comes out, then the date moves, and I would rather say that now than in three weeks. I can put the current contents and the estimates in front of you this afternoon, so the exchange rests on evidence rather than impressions. Which would you like to decide first?
commonMistakes: Refusing the request outright instead of stating the exchange
Accepting the additions and letting the date slip silently
variants: Answer again when the stakeholder says all five are mandatory.
